ShortDescription.Value: Take control of your city's horizon. Set custom district height limits to create smooth, natural transitions from suburbs to downtown. Fully configurable with no extra mod dependencies.

Publish.LongDescription:
District Height Policy
Create the perfect skyline height for your city! District Height Policy allows you to create custom districts and assign specific height limits to make your city's height transitions completely seamless.
Everything is easy to tweak—you can adjust all values directly yourself in the Settings menu. This mod has no dependencies.
How It Works
Height Checking: When a building spawns, the mod calculates its height against the policy set for that district. If it fits within the limit, it spawns; if it’s too tall or short, it is removed so another prefab can take its place.
Smart Fallback System: If no building fits the zone type or plot size for a strict policy, the mod gives up on that lot after 10 rerolls (configurable) and applies the Fallback System you picked in the Settings menu. Dezone Plot (the default) removes the zoning from the lot so it stays empty instead of holding a building that breaks your policy. Keep Building is the old behaviour: whatever last spawned is kept. (For example, no High Density Residential building exists for the "Small" policy, so those plots get dezoned rather than filled with a tower.)
Tips for Best Results
Maintain Asset Diversity: Strictly limiting height can restrict the variety of assets that spawn. It is highly suggested to use at least two height preferences or mix multiple zone types across your districts for a more diverse, natural look.
Optimize Lot Sizes: Sometimes manually deleting assets to trigger better plot size generation works wonders to improve your overall city aesthetics!
Note!: The mod is only designed to work for Residential zone type.

ChangeLog.Value: Added a Fallback System option in the Settings menu, by popular request. When a lot runs out of rerolls without producing a building that fits your district's policy, you can now choose what happens: Dezone Plot (the new default) removes the zoning from that lot so it stays empty, or Keep Building preserves the old behaviour of keeping whatever spawned.
